title: Postmortem: INT8 regression investigation
content:
TL;DR: after the last runtime change (kernel selection refactor), a small subset of long-context generation jobs started returning NaNs / garbage with INT8 quantized kernels. BF16 path OK. Repro rate ~2-5% on canary workloads, deterministic with seed in our local repro. Not yet confident whether this is a numeric stability edge (range/scale overflow) or a bug in the new fused-attn INT8 kernel path that mishandles denormals.

Timeline
- 2025-11-18: Canary rollout of kernel-refactor v0.9.2 (PR GH#4321) begins.
- 2025-11-19: Observed first user report: low-rate NaNs in hosted API for model rdl-7b-int8.
- 2025-11-20: Internal alert: spike in token decoding errors, correlation with long seq (>1024) and streaming enabled.
- 2025-11-21: Reproduction locally reproduced with deterministic script (see reproduction steps).

Repro steps (local - dockerized)
1) git checkout 0a3c9b1 (commit that introduced kernel selection refactor)
2) docker build -t rinf-int8-debug:local -f Dockerfile.debug .
3) docker run --gpus all -e RINF_MODELS=/models -v $PWD/models:/models -it rinf-int8-debug:local /bin/bash
4) inside container:
   export PYTHONPATH=/app
   python tests/repro/int8_regress_repro.py --model rdl-7b --quant int8 --seed 12345 --seq_len 1536 --batch 1 --stream

Observed output (snippet)
--- stdout ---
step 0: init kv cache OK
step 10: generating tokens...
Token 73: 0.345 0.122 0.987 -0.14 NaN NaN NaN
Floating point exception (core dumped)
--- end ---

Stack / logs (trimmed)
- runtime: selecting kernel fused_attn_int8_v2 for layer 6
- kernel: quant_conv: scale min=1.6e-08, max=8.1e+03
- warning: detected subnormal writes to output buffer at offset 0x7f12ab
- runtime: fallback to bf16 disabled for this customer profile

Commands tried (and results)
- Re-ran with O0 compiler flags: same repro.
- Forced fallback to v1 kernel (pre-refactor): no NaNs observed -> points to kernel change.
- Enabled denormals-preserve flags (FE_OPERATION): decreased repro rate but did not eliminate.
- Inserted tiny clamp at softmax input ([-50,50]): eliminated NaNs in local test -> suggests overflow in softmax exp path.
- Requantize with per-channel scales instead of per-tensor: reduced frequency but still occasional NaN.
- Seed sweep: reproducible for seed 12345, 67890; not for 22222 -> suggests RNG/initialization interacts.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) softmax exp overflow due to aggressive scaling in int8 path; quantized exponent implementation not handling extreme logits (likeliest).
2) denormal flushing policy on some GPUs leads to underflow/NaN when combined with fused kernel optimizations.
3) KV cache write race when using streaming + continuous batching produces corrupted buffer values (less likely since bf16 unaffected).
4) compiler vectorization combined with int8 packed layout produces an index math bug for certain sequence lengths (edge-case).

Quick checks to confirm/deny
- Reproduce with identical commit but run on different GPU arch (A100 vs H100). If only A100 shows it -> hardware-denorm interaction.
- Run with FENV settings to force denormals-as-zero (and opposite). Compare.
- Add per-layer instrumentation that emits max/min of logits pre-softmax (cheap running average).
- Run with single-threaded kernel loop to eliminate vectorization race.

Small experiment matrix (results summary)
- config: int8-per-tensor + fused_attn_int8_v2 + stream ON + seed 12345 -> 3/100 runs NaN
- config: int8-per-channel + fused_attn_int8_v2 + stream ON + seed 12345 -> 1/100 runs NaN
- config: int8-per-tensor + fused_attn_int8_v1 (pre-refactor) -> 0/100
- config: bf16 + fused_attn_bf16_v2 -> 0/200
- config: int8-per-tensor + fused_attn_int8_v2 + clamp([-50,50]) -> 0/200

Partial root-cause note
- The clamp workaround stops NaNs; that supports overflow in exp. But why do logits reach huge magnitude only on v2? v2 includes a fused QKV scaling + rotary + softmax compute path where intermediate accumulation uses int32 accumulators that are then requantized to int8 for softmax input. Suspect requantize step uses a scale factor computed from global max across batch, which under some streaming KB cache patterns is stale (old) and causes temporary large scaled logits.

Immediate mitigations (safe, low-risk)
- Disable fused_attn_int8_v2 for all hosted int8 models until further notice. (rolled to 100% rollback 2025-11-22)
- Add server-side clamp at softmax inputs in runtime as a short-term mitigation for int8 paths.

Longer-term actions
- Add per-layer rolling max/min metrics and alerts when softmax inputs exceed threshold (owner: Marco).
- Add unit tests that simulate streaming cache re-use and verify scale recompute correctness (owner: Priya).
- Audit quant->dequant/requant math in fused path for off-by-one index math and integer overflow.
- Plan: implement per-channel requantization by default for fused path if it doesn't materially regress perf.

Notes to self / open threads
- Check if JIT/LLVM vectorization flags changed around commit 0a3c9b1; maybe triggered a different loop layout.
- Verify math in exp approximator used in int8 softmax (look for table lookup out-of-bounds).
- Re-run repro under sanitizers (ASAN/UBSAN) in CPU emulation - may be noisy but worth a try.
- Keep an eye on low-frequency user reports after rollback; regression seems mostly mitigated but confirm in prod.

Short checklist for next 48h
- [ ] Re-run repro across GPU types (A100/H100/V100) and record exact repro rates.
- [ ] Add softmax input telemetry and ship to canary.
- [ ] Draft postmortem doc for eng-summit (include timeline + mitigations).
- [ ] Close GH#4321 with a clear revert and follow-up plan.

If you pick this up later: search for "fused_attn_int8_v2" in runtime logs and grep for "subnormal" and "softmax" tags. Keep seed 12345 handy.

Random small notes (brain dump)
- Maybe try low-precision exp with safe-guard: use bf16 for exp table calc then requantize.
- Could be better to recompute scale per-stream-chunk rather than per-request to avoid stale scales with streaming.

End of file.
